EC1: Patient [NOT] not expected to survive more than 4 days
EC2: Patient allergic to a penicillin [OR] or a carbapenem
EC3: Patient with significant polymicrobial bacteraemia (that is, a Gram positive skin contaminant in one set of blood cultures is not regarded as significant polymicrobial bacteraemia).
EC4: Treatment is not with the intent to cure the infection (that is, palliative care is an exclusion).
EC6: Use of concomitant antimicrobials in the first 4 days after enrolment with known activity against Gram-negative bacilli ([NOT] except trimethoprim/sulphamethoxazole may be continued as Pneumocystis prophylaxis).
EC7: Severe acute illness as defined by Pitt bacteraemia score of >4
EC8: Likely source to be from (proven or suspected at the time of randomisation) the central nervous system, e.g. brain abscess [OR], post-surgical meningitis [OR], shunt infection (due to concerns over CNS penetration of piperacillin/tazobactam)
